title: The leaky integrate-and-fire neuron solved exactly
promptMarkdown:
The leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) model of W1D1 Tutorial 2 (bonus section) is
$$\tau_m\frac{dV}{dt} = -(V - E_L) + RI,$$
with a spike emitted when $V$ reaches $V_{th}$, after which $V$ is reset to $V_{reset}$ and held for an absolute refractory period $t_{ref}$. All runs of this model are simulations; it is a mechanistic ('how') model.

1. For constant input current $I$ and $V(0) = V_{reset}$, solve the equation. What value does $V$ approach, and with what time constant?
2. Derive the condition on $I$ for the neuron to fire at all, and give the threshold current (the rheobase) in terms of the parameters.
3. For $I$ above rheobase, derive the time $T$ from reset to threshold and hence the firing rate $f = 1/(t_{ref} + T)$. What is the maximum firing rate the model can produce, and why?
4. Take $E_L = -70$ mV, $V_{th} = -50$ mV, $V_{reset} = -65$ mV, $\tau_m = 10$ ms, $R = 10\ \text{M}\Omega$, $t_{ref} = 2$ ms and $I = 3.0$ nA. Compute the rheobase, $T$ in ms and $f$ in Hz.
5. Name two observations about real neurons that this model cannot reproduce, and say which component you would have to add for each. (Do not describe any experiment on animals; name the observation only.)
hintLadder: Write $V_\infty = E_L + RI$. Then $u = V - V_\infty$ satisfies $\tau_m\,du/dt = -u$.
The neuron fires if and only if the asymptote lies above threshold. Solve $E_L + RI_{rh} = V_{th}$ for $I_{rh}$.
Set $V(T) = V_{th}$ in your solution and solve for $T$; it involves a logarithm of a ratio of voltage differences.
As $I \to \infty$, $T \to 0$, so the rate is bounded by the refractory period alone.
Think about what happens to a real neuron's rate under a long constant current, and about what shapes a real action potential.

deterministicChecks.description: the time-to-threshold formula contains a logarithm
the solution must be derived in general before numbers are substituted

criteria.criterion: V(t) = V_∞ + (V_reset − V_∞)e^{−t/τ_m} with V_∞ = E_L + RI, approached with time constant τ_m.
Fires iff E_L + RI > V_th; I_rh = (V_th − E_L)/R.
T = τ_m ln[(V_∞ − V_reset)/(V_∞ − V_th)]; f = 1/(t_ref + T); maximum rate 1/t_ref as I → ∞ because T → 0.

checkExamples.label: correct derivation
checkExamples.text: Let V_∞ = E_L + RI. For arbitrary constant I, u = V − V_∞ obeys τ_m du/dt = −u, so V(t) = V_∞ + (V_reset − V_∞) e^{−t/τ_m}, approaching V_∞ with time constant τ_m. The neuron fires iff V_∞ > V_th, i.e. I > I_rh = (V_th − E_L)/R. Setting V(T) = V_th: T = τ_m ln((V_∞ − V_reset)/(V_∞ − V_th)), and f = 1/(t_ref + T); as I → ∞, T → 0 and f → 1/t_ref. Numbers: I_rh = 20 mV/10 MΩ = 2.0 nA; V_∞ = −70 + 30 = −40 mV; T = 10 ln(25/10) = 9.16 ms; f = 1/(11.16 ms) = 89.6 Hz. Omissions: spike-frequency adaptation (add an adaptation current) and the action-potential waveform (add Hodgkin–Huxley conductances).

checkExamples.label: rate assumed proportional to current
checkExamples.text: The rate is f = I/(C V_th) which gives 150 Hz for 3 nA; rheobase is zero since any current eventually charges the membrane.
